answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil swarms by making reputation accrue as slowly as a glacier. Each new identity must lock a stake that only converts into voting weight after months of peer-attested work. A public atlas records which wallets funded which agents, so a thousand clones traced back to one funding jetty share a single, diluted score. For the attacker, every fake identity multiplies both the locked collateral and the waiting time, while an honest agent pays that price only once.
